subject: 1. THE NATIONAL MARITIME INTELLIGENCE CENTER (NMIC) ADVISES THAT PIRACY
text:
1. THE NATIONAL MARITIME INTELLIGENCE CENTER (NMIC) ADVISES THAT PIRACY
   HAS RESUMED IN INTERNATIONAL SHIPPING LANES OFF THE CENTRAL EAST COAST
   OF SOMALIA AS OF 14 MAY 2007. VESSELS REPORT BEING FIRED UPON APPROXIMATELY
   190 NM OFF THE SOMALI COAST IN THE VICINITY OF 01-20N 049-00E BY GUNMEN IN
   SMALL WHITE SPEEDBOATS ARMED WITH MACHINE GUNS AND ROCKET PROPELLED GRENADES.
   GIVEN THE DISTANCE FROM SHORE THESE RECENT ATTACKS HAVE OCCURRED AND POOR
   WEATHER CONDITIONS TYPICAL FOR THIS TIME OF YEAR, ONI ASSESSES PIRATES ARE
   LIKELY UTILIZING A LARGER MERCHANT VESSEL AS A MOTHER-SHIP TO LAUNCH THEIR
   SMALL-BOAT ATTACKS. THE INTERNATIONAL MARITIME BUREAU (IMB) HAS INCREASED
   THEIR RECOMMENDED TRANSIT DISTANCE FROM 75 NM TO 200 NM FOR VESSELS NOT CALLING
   ON SOMALI PORTS.
2. ONI FURTHER ADVISES VESSELS TO STAY AT LEAST 50 NM AWAY FROM POSITION
   01-02N 048-10E UNTIL THE MOTHER-SHIP THREAT CAN BE EVALUATED.
3. ALL VESSELS ARE ADVISED TO REMAIN AT LEAST 200 NM FROM THE EAST COAST OF
   SOMALIA.
   ALL MERCHANT VESSELS TRANSITING THE COAST OF SOMALIA, NO MATTER HOW FAR
   OFFSHORE, SHOULD INCREASE ANTI-PIRACY PRECAUTIONS AND MAINTAIN A HEIGHTENED
   STATE OF VIGILANCE.
   PIRATES ARE REPORTED TO HAVE USED PREVIOUSLY HIJACKED SHIPS AS BASES FOR
   FURTHER ATTACKS.
4. ANOTHER REPORTED PIRATE TACTIC HAS BEEN TO ISSUE A FALSE DISTRESS CALL TO LURE
   A SHIP CLOSE INSHORE. THEREFORE, CAUTION SHOULD BE TAKEN WHEN RESPONDING TO
   DISTRESS CALLS KEEPING IN MIND IT MAY BE A TACTIC TO LURE A VESSEL INTO A TRAP.
5. VICTIMIZED VESSELS REPORT TWO TO THREE 6 TO 9 METER SPEEDBOATS WITH 3 TO 6 ARMED
   MEN PER VESSEL ARMED WITH AK-47S AND SHOULDER LAUNCHED ROCKETS, OPENING FIRE ON
   THEIR VESSELS IN BROAD DAYLIGHT IN ORDER TO INTIMIDATE THEM INTO STOPPING.
6. TO DATE, VESSELS THAT INCREASE SPEED AND TAKE EVASIVE MANEUVERS AVOID BOARDING
   WHILE THOSE THAT SLOW DOWN ARE BOARDED, TAKEN TO THE SOMALI COASTLINE, AND
   RELEASED AFTER SUCCESSFUL RANSOM PAYMENT, OFTEN AFTER PROTRACTED NEGOTIATIONS
   OF AS MUCH AS 11 WEEKS.
7. FOR FURTHER INFORMATION REGARDING THIS ADVISORY, CONTACT THE MARITIME ADMINISTRATION,
   OFFICE OF SECURITY, CODE MAR-420, 2W23-312, 1200 NEW JERSEY AVE, SE, WASHINGTON, DC
   20590; TELEPHONE 202-366-1883, OR BY E-MAIL TO  OWEN.DOHERTY@DOT.GOV.
8. SUSPECTED ACTIVITY OR ACTUAL PIRACY/TERRORIST INCIDENT REPORTING GUIDANCE IS

THE FOLLOWING TRAFFIC SEPARATION SCHEMES (TSS),
PRECAUTIONARY AREAS, DESIGNATED ROUTES, NAVIGATIONAL
AIDS, AND REGULATIONS EFFECTIVE 010001Z JUL:
1. SUNK CENTER LIGHT VESSEL WITH RACON 51-50.1N 001-46.0E,
   NAVIGATION PROHIBITED WITHIN 0.5 MILES OF LIGHT.
2. SUNK OUTER PRECAUTIONARY AREA, ABOUT 12 MILES
   LONG, SIX MILES WIDE, CENTERED ON SUNK CENTER LIGHT
   VESSEL (51-50.1N 001-46.0E). ALL VESSELS ENTERING
   THIS AREA MUST FOLLOW THE RECOMMENDED COUNTER-CLOCKWISE
   TRAFFIC DIRECTION AROUND THE LIGHT VESSEL.
3. SUNK TSS NORTH IS SITUATED ADJACENT TO THE NORTH
   SIDE OF SUNK OUTER PRECAUTIONARY AREA, BETWEEN
   INNER GABBARD AND SHIPWASH. BEYOND THIS TSS, THE
   COASTAL ROUTE LEADS IN A NORTH DIRECTION ALONG
   THE EAST COAST OF ENGLAND.
4. SUNK TSS EAST IS SITUATED ADJACENT TO THE EAST SIDE
   OF SUNK OUTER PRECAUTIONARY AREA, BETWEEN INNER
   GABBARD AND THE GALLOPER. BEYOND THIS TSS, THE ROUTE
   LEADS IN AN EAST-NORTHEAST DIRECTION TO THE
   VICINITY OF NORTH HINDER JUNCTION PRECAUTIONARY AREA.
5. SUNK TSS SOUTH IS SITUATED ADJACENT TO THE SOUTH
   SIDE OF SUNK OUTER PRECAUTIONARY AREA, BETWEEN
   KENTISH KNOCK AND NORTH FALLS. BEYOND THIS TSS,
   ROUTES LEAD SOUTH-SOUTHEAST THROUGH FALLS GAP OR
   SOUTH-SOUTHWEST TO DOVER STRAIT TSS.
6. SUNK INNER PRECAUTIONARY AREA IS SITUATED ADJACENT
   TO THE WEST SIDE OF SUNK OUTER PRECAUTIONARY AREA.
   THIS AREA IS ABOUT SIX MILES LONG, SIX MILES WIDE,
   AND IS IRREGULAR IN SHAPE.
7. SUNK INNER LIGHTED BUOY  WITH RACON, IS MOORED IN
   POSITION 51-51.0N, 001-34.9E,
   NEAR THE CENTER OF SUNK INNER PRECAUTIONARY AREA.
8. GALLOPER RECOMMENDED ROUTE LEADS IN AN EAST-SOUTHEAST
   DIRECTION FROM THE SOUTHEAST SIDE OF SUNK OUTER
   PRECAUTIONARY AREA. THIS ROUTE IS DESIGNATED FOR
   CROSS-CHANNEL FERRIES PROCEEDING TO OR FROM OOSTENDE
   OR ZEEBRUGGE. SUCH FERRIES CROSS NOORD HINDER SOUTH
   TSS IN THE VICINITY OF TWIN LIGHTED BUOY (51-32.0N, 002-22.6E).
9. SHIPWASH BANK ROUTE LEADS SOUTH INTO SUNK INNER
   PRECAUTIONARY AREA (AVOIDING SUNK OUTER PRECAUTIONARY AREA).
   IT PASSES WEST OF SUNK TSS NORTH AND EAST OF SHIPWASH.
   ACCESS IS VIA A RESTRICTED AREA; VESSELS SHOULD NOTE THAT
   IT IS PROHIBITED TO ENTER OR EXIT THE HARWICH DEEP-WATER
   CHANNEL BETWEEN SOUTH SHIPWASH LIGHTED BUOY
   (51-52.7N, 001-34.2E) AND WALKER LIGHTED BUOY, MOORED
   ONE MILE NORTH. THIS ROUTE MAY BE USED BY VESSELS OF LESS
   THAN 20M IN LENGTH, SAILING VESSELS, AND VESSELS ENGAGED
   IN FISHING IRRESPECTIVE OF PORT OF DESTINATION OR ORIGIN.
   IT MAY ALSO BE USED BY VESSELS OPERATED UNDER A PILOTAGE
   EXEMPTION CERTIFICATE AND VESSELS EXEMPT FROM PILOTAGE BY
   THE REGULATIONS OF THE PORT OF DESTINATION. ALL SUCH VESSELS
   MAY PROCEED TO OR FROM ANY PORT ACCESSIBLE BY SUNK INNER
   PRECAUTIONARY AREA, INCLUDING THAMES AND MEDWAY PORTS.
10. LONG SAND HEAD TWO-WAY ROUTE, WHICH IS ABOUT 11 MILES LONG,
    LEADS NORTH INTO SUNK INNER PRECAUTIONARY AREA, CLOSE EAST
    OF LONG SAND HEAD (51-46N, 001-37E). IT PASSES BETWEEN
    KENTISH KNOCK AND THE WEST SIDE OF SUNK TSS SOUTH. THIS
    ROUTE MAY BE USED BY VESSELS OF LESS THAN 20M IN LENGTH,
    SAILING VESSELS, AND VESSELS ENGAGED IN FISHING IRRESPECTIVE
    OF PORT OF DESTINATION OR ORIGIN. IT MAY ALSO BE USED BY
    VESSELS OPERATED UNDER A PILOTAGE EXEMPTION CERTIFICATE
    AND VESSELS EXEMPT FROM PILOTAGE BY THE REGULATIONS OF THE
    PORT OF DESTINATION, WHICH ARE PROCEEDING ONLY
    TO OR FROM THAMES OR MEDWAY PORTS. IN ACCORDANCE WITH RULE
    NINE (72 COLREGS), VESSELS OF LESS THAN 20M IN LENGTH,
    SAILING VESSELS, AND VESSELS ENGAGED IN FISHING USING THIS
    ROUTE SHALL NOT IMPEDE THE PASSAGE OF A VESSEL WHICH CAN
    SAFELY NAVIGATE ONLY WITHIN THE NARROW CHANNEL OR FAIRWAY.
11. VESSELS WHICH ARE NOT PROCEEDING TO OR DEPARTING FROM
    PORTS WITHIN THE THAMES ESTUARY OR HARWICH HAVEN SHALL
    AVOID SUNK INNER PRECAUTIONARY AREA.
12. VESSELS NAVIGATING WITHIN SUNK INNER PRECAUTIONARY AREA
    SHALL AVOID IMPEDING THE PASSAGE OF A VESSEL CONSTRAINED
    BY DRAFT OR FOLLOWING A DEEP-WATER ROUTE.
13. SUNK VESSEL TRAFFIC SERVICE (VTS) SYSTEM OPERATES IN THE
    VICINITY OF SUNK CENTER LIGHT VESSEL AND COVERS SUNK OUTER
    PRECAUTIONARY AREA, SUNK INNER PRECAUTIONARY AREA, THE
    ASSOCIATED TSS, AND THE OTHER ROUTES LEADING INTO THESE AREAS.
    ALL VESSELS OF 300 GRT AND OVER SHALL PARTICIPATE IN THIS SYSTEM.
    AN EXTRACT OF SUNK VTS RULES IS LISTED BELOW:
    A. VESSELS MUST MAINTAIN A LISTENING WATCH WHEN WITHIN THE SUNK
       VTS AREA. THEY MUST ALSO REPORT TO SUNK VTS ON VHF CHANNEL
       14 WHEN ENTERING OR DEPARTING THE AREA AND WHEN
       PASSING THE DESIGNATED REPORTING POINTS.
    B. WHEN INITIALLY REPORTING TO SUNK VTS, VESSELS MUST STATE
       THEIR NAME, CALL SIGN, POSITION, DRAFT, DESTINATION, INTENDED
       ROUTE, AND ETA AT THE PILOT BOARDING STATION IF APPLICABLE.
    C. VESSELS IN THE AREA MUST REPORT TO SUNK VTS ANY INCIDENT
       THAT AFFECTS THE SAFETY OF NAVIGATION.
    D. VESSELS MUST MAINTAIN THEIR LISTENING WATCH UNTIL FINALLY
       CLEAR OF THE SUNK VTS AREA OR WHEN TRANSFERRING TO A
       NEIGHBORING VTS SYSTEM.
    E. VESSELS MUST REPORT TO SUNK VTS WHEN ANCHORING WITHIN THE
       AREA AND MAINTAIN A LISTENING WATCH.
    F. FISHING VESSELS ENGAGED IN FISHING MUST REPORT THEIR
       INTENTIONS TO SUNK VTS ON ENTERING OR LEAVING SUNK INNER
       PRECAUTIONARY AREA.
14. SUNK VTS SYSTEM AND ALL OF THE ABOVE TSS, PRECAUTIONARY AREAS,
    AND ROUTES LEADING INTO THEM ARE IMO-ADOPTED. WITH THE
    PRECAUTIONARY AREAS, THE INTERNATIONAL REGULATIONS FOR PREVENTING
    COLLISIONS AT SEA (72 COLREGS) APPLY.
15. SUNK PILOTS BOARDING STATION IS LOCATED IN POSITION
    51-51.4N 001-40.5E, ABOUT 3.5 MILES WEST-NORTHWEST OF SUNK
    CENTER LIGHT VESSEL. IT PROVIDES PILOTS FOR THE THAMES ESTUARY,
    HARWICH, FELIXSTOWE, IPSWICH, AND MISTLEY (HAVEN PORTS).
    THIS BOARDING STATION, WHICH MAY BE CONTACTED ON VHF, IS
    LOCATED WITHIN THE SUNK VTS AREA AND IN THE NORTHEAST PART
    OF SUNK INNER PRECAUTIONARY AREA. PILOTS AT THIS STATION
    ARE NORMALLY EMBARKED OR DISEMBARKED BY THE FOLLOWING:
    A. VESSELS WITH DRAFTS OF SIX METERS OR MORE ENTERING FROM
       OR LEAVING FOR PORTS TO THE NORTH AND NORTH EAST OF THE THAMES.
    B. VESSELS ENTERING FROM OR LEAVING FOR PORTS TO THE SOUTH AND
       EAST OF THE THAMES, WHICH ARE UNABLE TO USE PRINCES CHANNEL
       OR FISHERMANS GAT BECAUSE OF THEIR OPERATING DRAFT.
    C. VESSELS WITH DRAFTS OF LESS THAN SIX METERS, WHICH AGREE
       TO PAY AN ADDITIONAL PILOTAGE CHARGE FOR SUCH SERVICE.
    D. VESSELS ENTERING FROM OR LEAVING FOR PORTS IN ESSEX OR SUFFOLK.
16. THE FOLLOWING REGULATIONS APPLY TO VESSELS INTENDING TO EMBARK
    A PILOT AT SUNK PILOTS BOARDING STATION:
    A. INBOUND VESSELS MUST APPROACH FROM SUNK OUTER PRECAUTIONARY AREA.
    B. VESSELS MUST ADHERE TO THE PILOT BOARDING TURN ORDER ISSUED BY SUNK VTS.
    C. VESSELS MUST AVOID WAITING IN THE VICINITY OF THE BOARDING STATION.
    D. VESSELS MUST EMBARK THE PILOT EAST OF STORM LIGHTED BUOY
       (51-52N, 1-38E) UNLESS INFORMED BY SUNK VTS.
    E. VESSELS MUST MAINTAIN A LISTING WATCH ON THE VTS WORKING CHANNEL
       DURING BOARDING OPERATIONS. VHF CHANNEL 06 MAY BE USED FOR
       DIRECT COMMUNICATION WITH THE PILOT LAUNCH DURING THE EMBARKATION
       PROCEDURE.
17. VESSELS SHOULD NAVIGATE WITH EXTREME CAUTION IN THE VICINITY OF
    SUNK CENTER LIGHT VESSEL, SUNK INNER PRECAUTIONARY AREA, AND THE
    APPROACHES TO HARWICH HAVEN DUE TO THE HIGH DENSITY OF DEEP-DRAFT
    VESSELS AND CROSSING TRAFFIC THAT MAY BE ENCOUNTERED.
18. WHEN NAVIGATING THE OUTER PASSAGE, WHICH IS ALSO KNOWN AS THE THROUGH
    ROUTE, ACROSS THE OUTER PART OF THE THAMES ESTUARY, SOUTHBOUND VESSELS
    USUALLY KEEP TO THE WEST SIDE OF THE PASSAGE. FROM THE NORTH PART
    OF THE NORTH SEA, VESSELS SHOULD PASS EAST OF ALDEBURGH NAPES
    (52-09N, 1-42E) AND PROCEED INTO SUNK TSS NORTH. THEY SHOULD CONTINUE
    IN A SOUTH DIRECTION THROUGH SUNK OUTER PRECAUTIONARY AREA,
    PASSING EAST OF SUNK PILOTS BOARDING STATION AND WEST OF SUNK CENTER
    LIGHT VESSEL, INTO SUNK TSS SOUTH. VESSELS SHOULD THEN STEER IN A
    SOUTH-SOUTHWEST DIRECTION TO KEEP WEST OF SOUTH FALLS SHOAL, PASSING EAST
    OF DRILL STONE LIGHTED BUOY (51-26.0N, 0001-43.0E) AND EAST OF
    NORTHEAST GOODWIN LIGHTED BUOY (51-20.0N, 001-34.0E). THEY SHOULD
    THEN ADJUST COURSE TO ENTER THE SOUTHBOUND LANE OF DOVER STRAIT TSS,
    PASSING WEST OF SOUTH FALLS LIGHTED BUOY AND EAST OF EAST GOODWIN
    LIGHT FLOAT (51-13.0N, 001-36.0E). THIS ROUTE ALSO CAN BE USED BY
    VESSELS PROCEEDING SSE THROUGH FALLS GAP IN ORDER TO CROSS DOVER STRAIT
    TSS IN THE VICINITY OF FOXTROT 3 LIGHTED BUOY (51-24.0N, 002-00.0E).
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONCERNING SUNK VTS, REPORTING POINTS, OTHER
NEIGHBORING VTS SYSTEMS, AND ADDITIONAL PILOTAGE BOARDING STATIONS FOR
THE THAMES ESTUARY AND HARWICH HAVEN, SEE PUB. 192 SAILING DIRECTIONS (ENROUTE)
NORTH SEA (SECTOR 4).

subject: DENMARK. STORE BAELT. BELTREP VESSEL TRAFFIC SERVICE (VTS) SYSTEM:
text:
DENMARK. STORE BAELT. BELTREP VESSEL TRAFFIC SERVICE (VTS) SYSTEM:
1. BELTREP VTS, A MANDATORY SYSTEM, COVERS THE NORTH
   AND CENTRAL PARTS OF STORE BAELT (GREAT BELT).
   THIS VTS SYSTEM WILL BE OPERATIONAL 010000Z JUL.
2. THE NORTH LIMIT OF THE VTS IN AREA BOUND BY
   56-00.0N 011-17.0E (SJAELLANDS ODDE),
   56-00.0N 010-56.0E (NEAR MARTHE FLAK),
   56-47.0N 010-387.0E (EAST COAST OF SAMSO),
   55-36.0N 010-38.0E (FYN).
3. THE SOUTH LIMIT OF THE VTS IN AREA BOUND BY
    55-12.0N 011-15.4E (STIGSNAES OIL PIER),
    55-08.4N 011-09.0E (ORESPIDS),
    55-05.0N 011-09.0E (SOUTH OF ORESPIDS),
    55-05.0N 010-56.1E (EAST COAST OF LANGELAND),
    55-00.0N 010-48.7E (WEST COAST OF LANGELAND),
    55-01.2N 010-44.0E (THURO REV LIGHTED BUOY).
4. THE VTS AREA IS DIVIDED INTO TWO SECTORS
   AT LATITUDE 55-35.0N. SECTOR ONE LIES NORTH OF
   THIS LATITUDE AND SECTOR TWO LIES TO THE SOUTH.
5. ALL VESSELS OF 50 GRT AND OVER AND ALL VESSELS
   WITH AN AIR DRAFT OF 15 METERS AND OVER MUST
   PARTICIPATE IN THIS VTS SYSTEM.
6. VESSELS IN SECTOR ONE SHOULD COMMUNICATE WITH
   THE VTS (CALL: GREAT BELT VTS) ON VHF CHANNELS
   16 AND 74. VESSELS IN SECTOR TWO SHOULD
   COMMUNICATE WITH THE VTS (CALL: GREAT BELT VTS)
   ON VHF CHANNELS 16 AND 11. ALL VESSELS IN THE
   VTS AREA MUST MAINTAIN A CONTINUOUS LISTENING WATCH.
7. THE LANGUAGE USED FOR COMMUNICATION SHALL BE ENGLISH.
   IMO-STANDARD MARINE PHRASES SHOULD BE USED
   WHERE NECESSARY.
8. VESSELS ENTERING THE VTS AREA MUST SUBMIT A
   FULL REPORT WHEN CROSSING THE LIMIT LINES OR
   ON DEPARTURE FROM A PORT WITHIN THE AREA.
9. VESSELS CROSSING THE LINE BETWEEN SECTOR ONE
   AND SECTOR TWO MUST SUBMIT A SHORT REPORT.
   THIS REPORT SHOULD INCLUDE THE VESSELS NAME,
   CALL SIGN, IMO NUMBER, AND POSITION.
10. ADDITIONAL REPORTS MUST BE MADE WHENEVER THERE
    IS A CHANGE IN NAVIGATIONAL STATUS OR CIRCUMSTANCES.
11. REPORTS TO THE VTS SHOULD BE MADE USING VHF VOICE
    TRANSMISSIONS. HOWEVER, VESSELS CAN FULFIL CERTAIN
    REPORTING REQUIREMENTS THROUGH THE USE OF AIS.
    THE FULL REPORT MAY BE SUBMITTED BY USING A
    COMBINATION OF VOICE AND NON-VERBAL MEANS.
    VESSELS MAY SELECT, FOR REASONS OF COMMERCIAL
    CONFIDENTIALITY, TO COMMUNICATE THAT PART OF
    THEIR REPORT WHICH PROVIDES INFORMATION ON THE
    NEXT PORT OF CALL BY NON-VERBAL MEANS PRIOR TO
    ENTERING THE AREA.
12. THE FULL REPORT TO THE VTS SHOULD USE THE
    FOLLOWING PREFIXES AND BE IN THE FOLLOWING IMO FORMAT:
    A. VESSEL: NAME, CALL SIGN, AND IMO NUMBER.
    C. POSITION: A FOUR-DIGIT GROUP FOR LATITUDE
       SUFFIXED WITH N AND A FIVE-DIGIT GROUP FOR
       LONGITUDE SUFFIXED WITH E.
    I. NEXT PORT OF CALL.
    L. ROUTE.
    O. DRAFT (IN METERS).
    Q. ANY DEFECTS OR DEFICIENCIES AFFECTING NAVIGATION
       OR MANEUVERABILITY.
    U. DEADWEIGHT AND AIR DRAFT.
13. INFORMATION OF INTEREST TO SHIPPING IN THE VTS
    AREA WILL BE GIVEN ON REQUEST OR WILL BE BROADCAST
    ON A VHF CHANNEL SPECIFIED BY THE VTS. PRIOR TO THE
    BROADCAST AN ANNOUNCEMENT WILL BE MADE ON VHF
    CHANNEL 16. ALL VESSELS IN THE AREA SHOULD LISTEN
    TO THE BROADCAST.
14. THE VTS CAN PROVIDE NAVIGATIONAL ASSISTANCE TO
    INDIVIDUAL SHIPS, INCLUDING THE RECOMMENDATION OF
    SUITABLE ANCHORAGES. SUCH ASSISTANCE WILL BE MADE
    ON VHF CHANNEL 10 OR OTHER CHANNELS AS ASSIGNED.

subject: FOLLOWING THE PRESENCE OF FOOT AND MOUTH DISEASE IN ONE AREA IN THE
text:
FOLLOWING THE PRESENCE OF FOOT AND MOUTH DISEASE IN ONE AREA IN THE
UK AND THE EU RESTRICTIONS ON THE EXPORT OF MEAT AND DAIRY PRODUCTS
FROM THE UK, THE UK GOVERNMENT HAS ADVISED THAT MEAT AND MEAT
PRODUCTS, MILK AND DAIRY PRODUCTS SOURCED WITHIN THE UK FOR
CONSUMPTION ONBOARD ANY VESSEL INCLUDING RECREATIONAL CRAFT SHOULD
NOT BE LANDED ABROAD NOR ANY WASTE STEMMING FROM CONSUMPTION OF
THESE PRODUCTS. THOSE VESSELS UNABLE TO RETURN THE WASTE TO THE UK
FOR SAFE DISPOSAL SHOULD INFORM THE RECEIVING PORT TO ENSURE THAT
LOCAL BIOSECURITY MEASURES ARE OBSERVED. THESE RESTRICTIONS WILL
APPLY UNTIL LIFTED BY THE EU.

subject: 1. MULTI-NATIONAL NAVAL CONTROL OF SHIPPING (NCS)
text:
1. MULTI-NATIONAL NAVAL CONTROL OF SHIPPING (NCS)
   AUTHORITIES ARE CONDUCTING AN EXERCISE FROM
   01 THRU 08 SEP. THE EXERCISE WILL BE
   ONGOING IN THE BROAD VICINITY OF APPROACHES TO
   PANAMA CANAL.
2. AN NCAGS REGION HAS BEEN DECLARED AS OF 01 SEP
   IN THE INTERNATIONAL AND COASTAL WATERS APPROACHING
   THE PANAMA CANAL. THE REGION WILL BE DISESTABLISHED
   AS OF 09 SEP.
3. MERCHANT AND COMMERCIAL SHIPS TRANSITING THESE AREAS
   MAY BE REQUESTED TO REPORT VESSEL INFORMATION
   UTILIZING FORMAT ALPHA REPORTING STRUCTURE AS OUTLINED
   IN ATP2(B) VOL 2 INCLUDING:
   A. SHIP NAME.
   B. CALLSIGN.
   C. E-MAIL ADDRESS OF VESSEL.
   D. TYPE OF SHIP (E.G. TANKER, CONTAINER, BULK, FISHING.).
   E. TYPE OF CARGO.
   F. LOCATION, COURSE AND SPEED AT TIME OF REPORTING.
   J. PREVIOUS PORT OF CALL.
   H. NEXT PORT OF CALL AND ETA.
   REPORTS SHOULD BE MADE TO THE SHIPPING COORDINATOR AT
   THE FOLLOWING E-MAIL ADDRESS: SCT@NAVYTELEX.US
4. SAFETY IS PARAMOUNT. NAVAL DIRECTION TO MERCHANT
   SHIPPING IS ADVISORY ONLY.  MERCHANT PARTICIPATION
   IS VOLUNTARY.
5. MERCHANT VESSELS INTERESTED IN VOLUNTARY PLAY SHOULD
   CONTACT JECG@NAVYTELEX.US.
6. VESSELS WITHIN THE NCAGS SHIPPING AREA DURING THE
   EXERCISE DATES WITH QUESTIONS OR CONCERNS CAN CONTACT
   THE NCAGS SHIPPING CONTROL TEAM (SCT) VIA THEIR PANAMA
   AGENTS OR AT SCT@NAVYTELEX.US.
7. FOR FURTHER INFORMATION REGARDING THIS ADVISORY, CONTACT
   MR. DOHERTY, MARITIME ADMINISTRATION, OFFICE OF SHIP OPERATIONS,
   CODE: MAR-420, ROOM 23W-312, 1200 NEW JERSEY AVE.,
   WASHINGTON, DC 20590, TELEPHONE 202-366-1883, OR
   INTERNET E-MAIL: OWEN.DOHERTY@DOT.GOV.

subject: 1. MARITIME TRAFFIC CONTROL EXERCISE 151200Z TO 261500Z OCT.
text:
1. MARITIME TRAFFIC CONTROL EXERCISE 151200Z TO 261500Z OCT.
   INSTRUCTIONS FOR PARTICIPATION IN TRANSAMERICA VI EXERCISE
   APPLY TO ALL MERCHANT VESSELS THAT WISH TO PARTICIPATE IN
   A. THE MENTIONED EXERCISE OF NAVAL CONTROL OF MARITIME TRAFFIC
      AND ARE IN THE FOLLOWING SITUATIONS:
      1. IN TRANSIT, ENTERING IN BRAZILIAN MARITIME AREA.
      2. IN TRANSIT, INSIDE BRAZILIAN MARITIME AREA, DEMANDING A
         BRAZILIAN OR FOREIGN PORT,
      3. MOORED IN BRAZILIAN PORT WITH ESTIMATED LEAVE DURING
         PERIOD OF EXERCISE.
   B. THE INFORMATION CONTAINED IN FORM FORMAT ALFA SHOULD BE
      TRANSMITTED, BY E-MAIL, TO OFFICER OF OPERATING CONTROL (OCA)
      IN THE AREA WHERE THE MERCHANT SHIP IS, WITH COPY TO
      COMCONTRAM, WHENEVER THE SHIP IS UNDER ONE OF THE THREE
      SITUATIONS DESCRIBED ABOVE.
   C. THE FORMAT ALFA FORM IS ALSO AVAILABLE IN SITE
      WWW.COMCONTRAM.MAR.MIL.BR WHERE THE PARTIES CONCERNED CAN
      DOWNLOAD IF FROM LINK EXERCICIO CNTM/TRANSAMIRICA/FORMATALFA
      OR DIRECTLY IN ADDRESS WWW.COMCONTRAM.MAR.MIL.BR/CONTRAM/TRANSAM.HTM
      IN PORTUGUESE AND ENGLISH LANGUAGES.
   D. INSTRUCTIONS FOR ELABORATION OF TEXT OF MESSAGE FORMAT ALFA:
      1. DATE CAN BE EXPRESSED FOR EXTENSIVE (18.JUL 06 21.00 UTC)
         OR BY DATE-TIME GROUP (DTG).
      2. DATE-TIME GROUP (DTG) SHOULD BE EXPRESSED IN TIME ZONE "ZULU"
         IN FOLLOWING FORMAT: DDHHHHMMMAAZ (182100JUL06Z).
   E. FORMAT ALFA, SECTION A:
      1. DATA OF SHIP.
      2. NAME OF SHIP.
      3. INDICATIVE INTERNATIONAL RADIO.
      4. TYPE OF SHIP.
      5. FLAG OF REGISTRATION.
      6. IMO NUMBER.
      7. PORT OF REGISTRATION.
      8. LENGTH.
      9. MOUTH.
      10. MAXIMUM DRAUGHT FOR PRESENTE VOYAGE.
      11. GROSS TONNAGE.
      12. SPEED.
      13. SPEED OF CRUISE.
      14. MAXIMUM SPEED.
      15. MINIMUM SPEED.
      16. MAIN CHARACTERISTIC OF MERCHANT SHIP FOR VISUAL RECOGNITION.
      17. MMSI NUMBER IDENTITY OF MOBILE MARITIME SERVICE.
      18. NAME OF COMMUNICATION STATION ON WATCH.
      19. INMARSAT TELEPHONE NUMBER.
      20. FAC-SIMILE NUMBER.
      21. INMARSAT TELEX NUMBER.
      22. NUMBER OF VALITY OF INMARSAT DATA TRANSMISSION.
      23. OTHER MEANS OF COMMUNICATION.
   F. FORMAT ALFA, SECTION B, DATA OF VOYAGE:
      1. INTENTION OF MOVEMENT AND DESCRIPTION OF VOYAGE.
      2. LAST VISITED PORT, COUNTRY, ETC.
      3. NEXT PORT OF DESTINY AND ETA.
      4. CURRENT POSITION.
      5. GDH AND POSITION OF ENTRANCE IN AREA, AND OTHER
         COORDINATES OF POINTS OF THE ROUTE, INSIDE THE AREA,
         IN AGREEMENT WITH THE PLAN OF VOYAGE (GDH-LATITUDE/LONGITUDE).
      6. POSITION AND GDH OF EXIT OF THE AREA.
   G. FORMAT ALFA, SECTION C, DATA OF SHIP OPERATOR:
      1. NAME.
      2. ADDRESS.
      3. E-MAIL.
      4. NUMBER OF TELEPHONE AND FAC-SIMILE OF THE OWNER.
   H. FORMAT ALFA, SECTION D, DATA OF CARGO:
      1. AMOUNT AND NATURE OF MAIN CARGO.
      2. NAME AND ADDRESS OF SENDER OF MAIN CARGO.
      3. ORIGIN.
      4. ADDRESSEE.
      5. FINAL DESINATION OF MAIN CARGO.
      6. SPECIAL CONDITIONS APPLICABLE TO PRESENT OPERATION,
         SUCH AS TO INFORM IF ANY PEOPLE OR CARGO THAT IS BEING
         TRANSPORTED IS SUBJECT TO UN-SANCTION INDICATING YES OR NO.
         IF YES, DESCRIBE THE SITUATION ON A SEPARATE PAPER.
    G. DATA SUPPLIED BY NAVAL AUTHORITY OF THE AREA:
       1. TRANSAMERICA VI EXERCISE.
       2. 151200Z TO 261500Z OCT.
       3. BRAZILIAN MARITIME AREA:
          A. NORTH MARITIME AREA, UNDER RESPONSIBILITY OF OCA
             BRASNORTE, IN AREA BOUND BY 04-30N 051-38W,
             12-00N 045-00W, 12-00N 035-00W,
             05-00S 020-00W, 18-30S 020-00W,
             18-30S 039-42W, AND COAST.
          B. SOUTH MARITIME AREA, UNDER RESPONSIBILITY OF OCA BRASSUL,
             IN AREA BOUND BY 18-30S 039-42W, 18-30S 020-00W,
             35-50S 020-00W, 35-50S 050-10W, 33-47S  053-22W
             AND THE COAST.
    H. COMPONENTS OF THE ORGANIZATION OF NAVAL CONTROL OF BRAZILIAN
       MARITIME TRAFFIC:
       1. COMMANDS OF NAVAL DISTRICTS.
       2. SHIPPINT OFFICE, ASSISTANT PORT AND AGENCIES OF PORTS.
       3. COMCONTRAM.
    I. ADDRESS FOR COMMUNICATION:
       1. NORTH MARITIME AREA, CORRESPONDING TO OCA BRASNORTE SALVADOR

subject: 1. THIS MARAD ADVISORY ALERTS MARINERS TO BE VIGILANT IN THE GULF OF ADEN.
text:
1. THIS MARAD ADVISORY ALERTS MARINERS TO BE VIGILANT IN THE GULF OF ADEN.
   A VESSEL HIJACKING IN THE GULF OF ADEN WAS REPORTED BY THE NATIONAL MARITIME
   INTELLIGENCE CENTER, OFFICE OF NAVAL INTELLIGENCE ON 28 OCT.
2. THE NATIONAL MARITIME INTELLIGENCE CENTER (NMIC) ADVISED THAT A CHEMICAL TANKER
   WAS ATTACKED AND HIJACKED ON 28 OCT AT 0330Z WHILE UNDERWAY IN POSITION
   13-05N 050-24E APPROXIMATELY 70NM NORTH OF CALUULA, SOMALIA.
3. ONI FURTHER ADVISES MARINERS TO BE ON HIGH ALERT WHEN TRANSITING THIS AREA,
   PARTICULARLY THROUGH TO THE END OF NOVEMBER, WHEN MILD WEATHER OF THE FALL
   TRANSITION PERIOD IS CONDUCIVE TO SMALL BOAT OPERATION.
4. FOR FURTHER INFORMATION REGARDING THIS ADVISORY, CONTACT THE MARITIME ADMINISTRATION,
   OFFICE OF SECURITY, CODE MAR-420, ROOM W23-312, 1200 NEW JERSEY AVE, SE, WASHINGTON,
   DC 20590; TELEPHONE 202 366 1883, OR BY E-MAIL TO OWEN.DOHERTY@DOT.GOV.
5. SUSPECTED ACTIVITY OR ACTUAL PIRACY/TERRORIST INCIDENT REPORTING GUIDANCE IS PROVIDED
   IN MARAD ADVISORY 05-01.
